diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here $\phi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a differentiable interaction kernel

issues.failure_explanation: For two agents with a positive constant interaction weight, the difference of their colours satisfies a linear equation of the form d(c_1-c_2)/dt=-a(c_1-c_2), so a nonzero initial difference decays exponentially but never becomes exactly zero at finite time. Thus differentiable consensus dynamics do not generally produce exact constant-intensity clusters in finite time.

failure_location.quote: Classical results for opinion dynamics models~\cite{MotschTadmor2014} ensure that, under mild assumptions on $\phi$, the solution converges to a finite number of clusters in finite time. These clusters correspond to distinct regions of $\Omega$ over which the grey intensity is constant

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace finite-time exact clustering by an asymptotic or tolerance-based statement and state hypotheses on the kernel that actually yield the chosen notion of clustering.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted finite-time quantization mechanism and its interpretation as exact constant-colour regions are unsupported.
issues.title: Finite-time formation of constant-intensity clusters is false for smooth consensus dynamics
issues.why_classification: A comparable clustering interpretation can survive, but only after materially weakening the time and exactness claims and supplying appropriate hypotheses.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\alpha > 0$. Then the functional $J : H^1(\Omega) \to \R$ in Definition \ref{def:cost_functional} has a unique global minimum.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:existence1 minimizes J over all of H^1(Ω), whereas the optimal-control problem minimizes its restriction to terminal states reachable from measurable controls. A unique unconstrained minimizer need not be reachable, and the theorem supplies neither existence of an optimal control nor compactness/closedness of the reachable terminal-state set.

failure_location.quote: We define a cost functional based on the $L^2$ norm of the intensity gradient, establish the well-posedness of the problem, and derive the corresponding optimality system.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove existence of an optimal control under explicit state, kernel, and control-topology assumptions, or withdraw the claim that the optimal-control problem is well posed and describe thm:existence1 only as an unconstrained variational result.
issues.overall_effect: The paper does not establish the advertised existence or well-posedness of the first optimal-control problem.
issues.title: Unconstrained minimization of J does not establish well-posedness of the optimal-control problem
issues.why_classification: The available local repair withdraws an advertised existence guarantee; preserving it requires a new optimal-control existence argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The state map is coupled: each F_i depends on multiple c_k. Integration by parts therefore produces the adjoint action (D_cF)^Tλ, whose kth component is the sum over i of λ_i ∂F_i/∂c_k. The displayed pointwise product does not express that transpose/nonlocal sum and is generally different from D_cF λ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the adjoint with the transpose of the full discrete Jacobian, or derive the corresponding nonlocal integral adjoint explicitly, and use that operator in the DAL routine.
issues.overall_effect: The stated optimality system and any implementation that follows its literal adjoint equation do not compute the reduced-cost gradient.
issues.title: The adjoint equation omits the transpose of the coupled-state Jacobian
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained to the adjoint derivation and implementation, but it is nontrivial and can change all computed controls.

issues.failure_explanation: Every Armijo test evaluates the projected candidate ε−τD, but the accepted update uses ε+τD. Consequently, the algorithm applies a point for which no decrease test was performed and, when D is the gradient used in the tests, moves in the ascent direction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Update with the same projected minus-direction candidate accepted by the line search, then rerun the numerical experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The DAL iteration is not a validated steepest-descent method, and the computed controls and all ADMM steps that call DAL are unreliable.
issues.title: DAL applies the opposite candidate from the one accepted by its line search
issues.why_classification: The code-level correction is local, but all reported optimization outputs must be recomputed because the literal algorithm may increase the objective.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $E$ be a convex, compact subset of $[0,+\infty)\times[0,+\infty)$.

issues.failure_explanation: At a boundary point, projection can give Π_E(ε−τD)=ε for every positive τ in an outward direction. The left side is then J(ε), while the right side is strictly smaller than J(ε) whenever D is nonzero, so the while-condition remains true for every backtracked step and the loop never terminates.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the test by a standard projected-gradient Armijo condition based on the actual projected displacement and include a stationary projected-step termination check.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:dal is not well defined for legitimate constrained iterates, including the box constraints used in the experiments.
issues.title: The projected Armijo test can loop forever at an active constraint
issues.why_classification: A standard contained redesign of the line search suffices, but more than a typographical change is required to restore termination and descent.

issues.failure_explanation: For j=i, the summand in F_i is identically φ(0)(c_i−c_i)=0, so its derivative with respect to c_i is zero. The stated diagonal formula nevertheless includes −φ(0)/N from that term; with the displayed kernel φ(0)=−1, this is explicitly nonzero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Exclude j=i from the diagonal sum, or differentiate the self-term with both occurrences of c_i accounted for, and recompute the adjoint-based experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The Jacobian supplied for the adjoint computation is wrong, so DAL does not use the derivative of the stated dynamics.
issues.title: The displayed state Jacobian differentiates the identically zero self-interaction incorrectly
issues.why_classification: The formula has a local correction, but it changes the implemented gradient and requires revalidation of all numerical outputs.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here $\phi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a differentiable interaction kernel that weighs the influence of neighbouring agents
where the compactly supported interaction kernel is given by the $C^2$ Wendland function
each agent tends to align its state $c_i$ with the states of nearby agents

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed polynomial has φ(0)=−1 and is negative for 0≤r<1/4, so nearby unequal agents are driven away from rather than toward each other. Moreover, because the second branch is zero for r<0 while the value at zero is −1, the declared function on R is discontinuous at zero, hence neither differentiable nor C2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify a nonnegative kernel with the asserted regularity and rerun all dynamics and optimization experiments using that corrected kernel.
issues.overall_effect: The literal dynamics do not have the claimed attractive interpretation, and the derivative formulas and numerical results may correspond to a different kernel than the one printed.
issues.title: The stated interaction kernel is repulsive near zero and is not the claimed differentiable C2 kernel
issues.why_classification: Although the formula may admit a short correction, the source does not force a unique repair and the kernel determines every reported numerical trajectory.

issues.failure_explanation: The term |v| is not differentiable at v=0, as also reflected by the subsequent casewise shrinkage formula. Introducing the auxiliary variable and quadratic penalty does not smooth this term.

failure_location.quote: In this way, we move from a minimum problem for $K$ to a saddle point problem for $L$, which is smooth.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that L remains nonsmooth in v but has a proximal/shrinkage update, rather than claiming smoothness.
issues.overall_effect: The stated rationale for replacing the nonsmooth problem is mathematically incorrect, though block minimization by shrinkage can still handle the nonsmooth term.
issues.title: The augmented TV functional is falsely claimed to be smooth
issues.why_classification: A short local correction preserves the functional, algorithmic strategy, and substantive guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: when approaching the minimum point $(u^*,v^*)$ in the primal variables (which is unique), the term $\int_\Omega \mu \cdot (v^*-\nabla u^*)$ vanishes, so that any $\mu \in L^2(\Omega; \R^2)$ becomes feasible.

issues.failure_explanation: Along the constraint v=∇u, the quadratic penalty vanishes and the objective controls only the L1 norm of ∇u and the L2 norm of u, not the H1 norm. Smoothed step functions can have bounded L2 norm and bounded integral of |∇u| while their L2 gradient norm diverges, so the claimed H1 coercivity and weak compactness do not follow. In addition, vanishing of the constraint term does not make every multiplier a saddle multiplier: minimization in v imposes a subgradient condition on μ.

failure_location.quote: Finally, as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:existence1}, it is immediate to show coercivity in the primal variables, ensuring that the minimum is attained in a weakly compact set. The ensemble of these properties is sufficient to guarantee the existence of a saddle point in our setting

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must choose function spaces in which the TV problem is compact, prove primal and dual attainment, and establish the required multiplier/subgradient conditions.
issues.overall_effect: Existence of a saddle point and the asserted strong-duality justification for the infinite-dimensional H1/L2 formulation are not established.
issues.title: The saddle-point existence proof relies on false H1 coercivity
issues.why_classification: The central saddle-point theorem requires new functional-analytic architecture; the proof's compactness mechanism fails in the stated spaces.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we lose convexity in the control-to-state map $\varepsilon \mapsto c(\,\cdot\,,T; \varepsilon)$, so we can only expect convergence to a local minimum in the first variable.
This is the reason why Theorem \ref{thm:saddle_point} is fundamental: it ensures that there is no duality gap.

issues.failure_explanation: Existence of a saddle point or absence of a duality gap does not supply convergence of an alternating method. The actual first block is a nonconvex control problem solved only locally by DAL, and no assumptions or argument establish convergence of the outer multiplier iteration to the unique global primal solution.

failure_location.quote: However, this does not pose an issue for the numerical algorithms, which will converge to the unique primal solution and to one of the optimal dual ones.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either provide a convergence theorem applicable to the inexact, nonconvex block updates used here, or explicitly present the method as a heuristic without a guarantee of convergence to the unique primal solution.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed convergence guarantee for the numerical method, and hence its asserted recovery of the TV primal solution, is unsupported.
issues.title: Saddle-point existence does not imply convergence of the proposed nonconvex numerical algorithms
issues.why_classification: The source supports no convergence proof for the proposed nonconvex nested iteration; the available repair withdraws a central guarantee type.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Start the loop at j=0 with consistently shifted output indices, or initialize μ^(1) and specify which multiplier is used in each block update.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:admm is not executable as written.
